subject: general
question: The monetary policy in India is formulated by the ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central banking institution of India, which controls the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• RBI was established on 1st April 1935, in accordance with the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• The primary objective of the RBI's monetary policy is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy**

 
 
• Monetary policy refers to the policy of the central bank aimed at regulating the supply of money and interest rates in the economy to achieve macroeconomic objectives such as controlling inflation, consumption, growth, and liquidity.
 
• In India, the RBI formulates and implements the monetary policy to ensure financial stability and to achieve the targets set by the government.
 
• Monetary policy tools include open market operations, the cash reserve ratio, statutory liquidity ratio, and repo rate among others.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**
 
 
• The RBI also acts as the regulator of the financial system, overseeing the functioning of various financial institutions in India.
 
• It acts as the banker to the Government of India and the state governments.
 
• RBI also manages the country's foreign exchange and gold reserves.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in the development of the financial infrastructure of the country, including the development of the payment and settlement systems.
 
 
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)**
 
 
• OMOs are conducted by the RBI to control the money supply in the economy by buying or selling government securities in the open market.
 
• When the RBI sells government securities, it absorbs liquidity from the market, and when it buys securities, it injects liquidity into the market.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate**
 
 
• The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks.
 
• A reduction in the repo rate helps banks get money at a cheaper rate, which in turn can help to lower the interest rates for borrowers.
 
• Conversely, an increase in the repo rate can help to control inflation by making borrowing more expensive.
